materials.title: At the school gate
materials.text:
Read the five short conversations. Choose the reply that completes each conversation.

1. Ben: Good morning, Amy!
Amy: ___

2. Amy: What's your name?
New boy: ___

3. Ben: How are you today?
Amy: ___

4. New boy: Is this your blue bag, Ben?
Ben: ___

5. Amy: Let's go to class.
Ben: ___

questions.explanation: 清晨见面的Good morning用同样问候回应。Good night用于夜间告别；年龄和物品回答不能回应问候。

questions.prompt:
Amy: What's your name?
New boy: ____
questions.explanation: What's your name询问姓名，My name is Leo直接回答。其余分别回答身体状态、颜色和一般疑问句，均不回答名字。

questions.prompt:
Ben: How are you today?
Amy: ____
questions.explanation: How are you询问状态，I'm fine, thank you合适。铅笔介绍、姓名及告别均与所问不符。

questions.prompt:
New boy: Is this your blue bag, Ben?
Ben: ____
questions.explanation: Is this your blue bag是确认归属的一般疑问句，Yes, it is作答并致谢自然。喜好、下午问候和年龄均未回答书包归属。

questions.prompt:
Amy: Let's go to class.
Ben: ____
questions.explanation: Let's go to class提出共同去教室，OK! Let's go接受建议。物品、姓名和对am/is人称问句的否认都不回应邀请。

materials.title: At the art table
materials.text:
Read the five short conversations. Choose the reply that completes each conversation.

1. May: What colour is your new crayon?
Jack: ___

2. Jack: May I use your red crayon, please?
May: ___

3. Jack: Thank you, May.
May: ___

4. May: Look at my picture!
Jack: ___

5. Jack: It's time to go home. Goodbye!
May: ___

questions.prompt:
May: What colour is your new crayon?
Jack: ____
questions.explanation: 问句明确询问crayon颜色，green回答颜色。ruler是物品，Jack是姓名，Good night是告别，均不匹配。

questions.prompt:
Jack: May I use your red crayon, please?
May: ____
questions.explanation: May I use请求借用蜡笔，Sure. Here you are同意并递物。年龄、动物命名和问候都没有回答请求。
Thank you之后You're welcome回应感谢。颜色、状态及姓名分别回答其他问题，不能在这里构成感谢应答。

questions.prompt:
May: Look at my picture!
Jack: ____
questions.explanation: Look at my picture邀请观看作品，赞赏作品beautiful自然。年龄、姓名和am问句肯定未回应作品展示。

questions.prompt:
Jack: It's time to go home. Goodbye!
May: ____
questions.explanation: 对方明确回家并Goodbye，Goodbye! See you tomorrow是告别回应。其余颜色、归属和状态答句不能完成此次告别。

materials.title: A shelf for another chance
materials.text:
Last winter, Mina put a small wooden shelf beside the front desk of her neighbourhood centre. A card above it said, 'Broken things may need a small repair, not a rubbish bin.' People could leave a broken household object on the shelf with a note explaining the problem. On Saturday mornings, volunteers tried to repair it.

At first, Mina expected mostly lamps and clocks. Instead, the shelf filled with schoolbags. Several had broken zips, but the cloth was still strong. One parent explained that buying a new bag was often easier than finding someone to repair a zip. Mina asked Rosa, a retired shop owner, to teach the volunteers basic sewing skills.

The volunteers did not promise to repair everything. They refused dangerous electrical work and returned objects they could not safely fix. When a repair needed a new part, they called the owner before spending any money. A repaired object stayed on a separate collection shelf for a week. If it was not collected, Mina contacted its owner again rather than giving it away.

After two months, Mina stopped counting only how many objects had been repaired. She also began counting how many people had learned a repair skill. One Saturday, a boy who had brought in a torn pencil case returned with his sister. This time, he showed her how to sew a small tear. Mina felt that the shelf was finally doing more than saving objects.

questions.prompt: What did people need to leave with a broken object?
options: A promise to become a volunteer.
questions.explanation: 首段直接要求a note explaining the problem，C准确。原文没有要求主人照片、购买新品的钱或志愿承诺。

questions.prompt: Why did Mina invite Rosa to help?
options: The centre needed a new front desk.
Rosa wanted to sell new schoolbags.
questions.explanation: 第二段先说书包拉链坏而布料结实，再请Rosa教basic sewing skills，A对应需求。前台不需要更换，未说售卖新包，危险电器工作反而被拒绝。

questions.prompt: What happened when a repair required a new part?
options: The volunteers bought it without asking.
The owner was contacted before money was spent.
The object was put straight into a rubbish bin.
The owner had to repair the object alone.
questions.explanation: 第三段明确called the owner before spending any money。A与先询问相反；C不是需要新零件的处理；D没有依据。

questions.prompt: What did Mina do if an object was not collected after a week?
options: She sold it to pay for repairs.
She gave it to another family.
questions.explanation: 第三段说明未领取时再次联系主人rather than giving it away，D正确；售卖、转赠或立即丢弃均不符合规则。

questions.prompt: Why was Mina pleased when the boy returned with his sister?
options: He had bought a more expensive pencil case.
He was passing on a skill he had learned.
His sister offered to build another shelf.
All the broken objects had been repaired.
questions.explanation: 末段男孩教妹妹缝小裂口，证明技能继续传递，B对应新增目标。未购买昂贵文具盒，未承诺建架，也没有所有物品均修好的结论。
